Blasted through the final stretch of Megaman Zero just now. Got a permanent F rank, but whatever; I already knew the score would be tanked by choosing the powerups (didn't realize by JUST HOW MUCH, but fine, whatever).

This was a different kind of Megaman experience, with only three elemental powers and four different (non-elemental) weapon types. The whole weakness system present in the main Megaman series was barely there, with only the element chips playing into that at all, and even then only after charging your weapon up. I know Zero obtained different weapons rather than elemental powers in the X games he was playable in, but each weapon still had a different effect on different enemies, so the element system was still in place albeit in a different form. Not so much here. Considering the base forms of each weapon are non-elemental, I guess they're more for player preference than anything else, because I only remember literally ONE instance where an enemy was immune to bullets. The vast majority of the game I just stuck with the Z-saber, not really caring for the other weapon types (no, I don't regret grinding them up anyway; that's part of the gameplay loop and it didn't take that long regardless). I wasn't impressed with the Shield Boomerang, so I have to wonder why they went and put it into all four games. I just hope it's better in the other titles, because it seemed by far the worst weapon here.

I absolutely did not care for the cyber-elf power up system. As far as I understand it, it's different in all four games, but I'm not sure to just what degree. I think finding powerups hidden throughout the level is a better design choice for this type of game. For that matter, I wasn't too big a fan of permanently losing access to areas after missions. I much prefer how level changing was done in the X series, like Flame Mammoth's stage being frozen over after you beat Chill Penguin in the first X game, not to mention just the fact that you can easily revisit completed areas.

Despite the gripes, it was overall still a fun experience. I'm not sure what I'll be getting to next just yet, but I had mentioned getting back to Final Fantasy VI not that long ago and Chrono Trigger's caught my eye again...
